timed out after 5m0.000306269s (excluding download) waiting for app "24d773e8-c752-4ab9-a84f-f2817cc37881" (diag-reader) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed: the `extract-*` snapshot is still `Active` (uncommitted) for the diag-reader image layer — exactly the unpack-stall signature. I have enough evidence now.

**Root cause:** `diag-reader`'s volume (`9ebd7ba3-ba11-49ea-9ec3-328d02fc7581`) entered `CREATING_VOLUME` and is still there live — `ctr snapshots ls` shows an `extract-601665617-P_cQ` snapshot still `Active` (uncommitted) for the image layer. Live `nproc`/`vmstat` on `edge-dev` show the classic CPU/IO-oversubscription signature seen repeatedly in this ledger: the guest reports only `nproc=1` against a device configured for 4 vCPUs, and `vmstat` shows a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`, `wa`≈24-26%). This is corroborated by `evetest broker status`: host `farfalle` is running 13/16 VMs at 102% of host RAM assigned with 1.9 GiB swap in use — the same oversubscription condition that has slowed image unpacks past the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→`RUNNING` budget throughout this ledger.

This is a **known, recurring issue**: `TestDiagOutput` (same test, same app `diag-reader`) failed with this identical `CREATING_VOLUME` timeout signature back on 2026-11-20 (run #30), where the conclusion then was also CPU-oversubscription-driven slow volume casting (that time it did eventually complete at 7m44s). It also matches the broader, heavily-recurring `CREATING_VOLUME`/unpack-stall-under-host-CPU-oversubscription class that has hit dozens of different tests/suites in nearly every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 — an infrastructure/environment issue, not a product regression. No PR diff was supplied for this investigation, so no relatedness judgment is given.

timed out after 5m0.000234767s (excluding download) waiting for app "af4a6ae7-50a2-46a2-93da-de8465477f7f" (app1) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
Host `farfalle` is at 102% of host RAM assigned to running VMs (13/16 VMs), 1.9 GiB swap in use, load 11.93/9.44/8.50 across 40 cores — the same oversubscription signature already confirmed for this run's earlier `TestProfile` and `TestAppLocalInfo` failures.

**Root cause:** `app1`'s root volume on `edge-dev` is still stuck in `CREATING_VOLUME` live (`ctr snapshots ls` shows one `Active`/uncommitted unpack snapshot `b0a8bdfb-...`, and `/persist/vault/volumes/` has no populated rootfs yet) well past the 5-minute deadline. The guest again exposes only `nproc=1` against its configured 4 vCPUs, with `vmstat` showing a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`, `wa`≈23-28%) just 11 minutes after boot, load average 3.65 — classic CPU/IO starvation during container-image unpack caused by host oversubscription, corroborated by the broker (`farfalle` at 102% of host memory assigned to running VMs, swap in use, load 11.93).

This is the identical root cause documented twice already in this same run (`TestProfile` and `TestAppLocalInfo` in `live-investigation.md`), and per `live-ledger.md` this is a known, heavily recurring infrastructure issue (slow/unpack-under-oversubscription causing the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→RUNNING timeout to trip) affecting many tests across nightly runs since at least 2026-11-20 — not a product regression in this test or EVE itself.

timed out after 5m0.001094485s (excluding download) waiting for app "4c57dcb4-9f55-4c40-ac68-63f59347cf6b" (lps-app) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed: four concurrent `extract-*` snapshots are still `Active` (uncommitted) on the device at 05:57:23, well past the 5-minute timeout, with the volumes directory empty — classic concurrent-unpack contention, not a single app. This matches all the live evidence.

**Root cause:** `lps-app`'s root volume is still stuck in `CREATING_VOLUME` (live `AppInstanceStatus` shows `State:109`) well past the 5-minute deadline, with live `ctr snapshots ls` showing four concurrent `extract-*` containerd snapshots still `Active`/uncommitted — multiple container-image unpacks competing for CPU at once. Live `nproc`/`vmstat`/`uptime` on `edge-dev` show the classic oversubscription signature: the guest exposes only `nproc=1` against a device configured for 4 vCPUs, load average 5.65 right after an 8-minute-old boot, and `vmstat` shows a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`, `wa`≈21-29%). `evetest broker status` corroborates this: the Proxmox host (`farfalle`) is running 13/16 VMs at 102% of host RAM assigned, with 1.9 GiB of swap in use and host load 7.2-8.2.

This is the identical root cause as the 2026-11-21 (run #35) occurrence of this exact test (`TestLPSSuite/TestProfile`), where the ledger records `lps-app`'s unpack taking ~2m32s amid concurrent volume creates and finishing just ~15s past the deadline — the same "slow-but-completing unpack under CPU oversubscription" pattern. It is also part of a much broader, heavily recurring class (concurrent container-image unpacks exceeding the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→RUNNING timeout under host CPU/IO oversubscription) that has hit dozens of different tests/suites in nearly every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 — an infrastructure/environment issue, not a product regression. No PR diff was provided for this investigation.

--- TestAppLocalInfo ---
timed out after 5m0.000217275s (excluding download) waiting for app "cf3f9f27-283a-4551-a051-7a2b0df51e7c" (app1) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
This corroborates: the broker host `farfalle` is at 86% memory assigned, swap in use (1.9 GiB), and load 8.0-8.2 across 40 cores — consistent with the device-level oversubscription signature (guest `nproc=1` vs. configured 4, `wa`≈24-28%) seen in `vmstat`.

### Root cause

This is the known "slow-but-completing container-image unpack under host CPU/IO oversubscription" pattern already documented twice earlier in this same run (`TestProfile` and an earlier `TestAppLocalInfo` entry in `live-investigation.md`/ledger). Live evidence: `CreateVolume`/`UnpackClientImage` for app1's root volume (`54426fc0-a7db-46b0-b0b4-06ae07e4d5aa`) started at 06:23:50.331, and `/persist/vault/volumes/54426fc0.../rootfs` is now (06:29) fully populated with the app progressing to `BOOTING` at 06:29:28 — a ~5m38s unpack, just past the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→RUNNING deadline, not a true hang. Live `nproc`/`vmstat` on `edge-dev` show the guest exposing only 1 vCPU against a device configured for 4, with `wa`≈24-28% and a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`); `evetest broker status` shows the Proxmox host `farfalle` at 86% of host memory assigned to running VMs, 1.9 GiB swap in use, and load 8.0-8.2 across 40 cores, corroborating oversubscription.

This shares the identical root cause as this run's earlier `TestProfile` failure recorded in `live-investigation.md`. Per `live-ledger.md`, this is a known, long-recurring issue dating back to at least the 2026-11-20 nightly (run #30), and this exact test (`TestLPSSuite/TestAppLocalInfo`) has failed with this same signature before, on 2026-11-21 (run #35) — this is at least the third occurrence of this specific test/failure combination.

--- TestMgmtTrafficRoutedViaApp ---
Told to stop trying after 17.927s.
Stop waiting for: ni-wan is ONLINE
Network instance is in error state
networkID:"5ef0dd1b-6474-4d0e-ad56-b4d2fdbe0351" networkVersion:"1" instType:1 displayname:"ni-wan" bridgeNum:1 networkErr:{description:"failed to select ports for network instance 5ef0dd1b-6474-4d0e-ad56-b4d2fdbe0351: no port is matching label 'ethernet0'" timestamp:{seconds:1795848396 nanos:259518971} severity:SEVERITY_ERROR} state:ZNETINST_STATE_ERROR mtu:1500

Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed self-healed: `ni-wan` is now `ZNETINST_STATE_ONLINE` with `ethernet0` correctly assigned to eth0.

**Root cause:** This is the same well-known boot-time DPC-promotion race documented repeatedly in the ledger for other tests, now hitting `TestMgmtTrafficRoutedViaApp` for the first time with this particular signature. Device `edge-dev` did its first boot at 06:45:22 and came up on the fallback `lastresort` DPC (bare `eth0`/`eth1`, no logical labels). The real `zedagent` DPC — which maps logical label `ethernet0`→`eth0` — was created at 06:46:23.645 but `nim` didn't start/finish its verification cycle until 06:46:34.977–06:47:04.328 (repeated restarts due to wwan/IP-address-change events). Zedrouter tried to resolve the NI's `ethernet0` port label at 06:46:36.259 and 06:46:44.104, both before the new DPC had been verified and promoted, logging `no port is matching label 'ethernet0'` exactly as seen in the failure. The test's fail-fast wait only budgeted 17.927s and gave up well before the DPC finished promoting at 06:47:04; live `evetest eve ni-info ni-wan` now confirms the NI is fully `ZNETINST_STATE_ONLINE` with `ethernet0` correctly assigned, confirming self-healing, not persistent misconfiguration.

This does not share a root cause with the other failures collected in this run (`TestDNSFunctionality`'s subscribe-after-send race, or the unrelated `bpftrace-compiler` SIGSEGV). Per the ledger, `TestMgmtTrafficRoutedViaApp` has failed twice before (run #35 2026-11-21, and run #66 2026-11-27 last night) but each time with a *different* mechanism (a firewall/DPC-fallback metrics-routing race), so this exact `no port is matching label` NI-error signature is new for this test — however it is simply another instance of the broader, long-standing "lastresort→zedagent DPC promotion racing a fail-fast NI-error wait" class that the ledger has recorded recurring across many suites since at least 2026-11-20 (run #30).

Claude's conclusion:
Still stuck in `CREATING_VOLUME` even now, confirming the stall persists live.

**Root cause:** `vlan20-app`'s volume is stuck in `CREATING_VOLUME` well past the 5-minute test timeout, and live inspection on device `edge-dev` shows the classic CPU/IO-oversubscription unpack-stall signature seen throughout this run's ledger: `nproc` reports only 1 usable CPU despite the device being configured for 4 vCPUs, `vmstat` shows a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1-2`, `wa`≈23-29%), and `ctr -n eve-user-apps snapshots ls` shows two `extract-*` snapshots still `Active` (uncommitted) for the app's image layer. The broker (`farfalle`) corroborates environmental contention (9/12 VMs running, 70% of host RAM assigned, 1.9 GiB swap in use, host load 4.66-6.60). This does **not** share a root cause with the earlier `TestMgmtTrafficRoutedViaApp` failure recorded in `live-investigation.md` (a self-healing boot-time DPC-promotion race), which is a different mechanism entirely. `TestVLANSubinterfaces` has appeared once before in the ledger (2026-11-25, run #55), but with a *different* failure mode (a DHCP-offer/SDN-model-switch race on `eth0`), so this specific `CREATING_VOLUME`-under-oversubscription signature is new for this test — it is, however, simply another instance of the broader, heavily recurring unpack-stall class that has hit dozens of tests in essentially every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 (run #30).

This matches the exact same signature documented repeatedly in the ledger.

**Root cause:** `passthrough-app`'s image layer (`extract-987005580-sicw`) is stuck as an `Active` (uncommitted) containerd snapshot right now — the app entered `CREATING_VOLUME` at 06:49:10 and never progressed past it through the full 5-minute timeout and beyond (still stuck at my live check, 06:52:31+). This is the only test in this suite run so far, so there's no earlier same-run failure to share this root cause with. It is a **known, heavily recurring issue** per the ledger: this exact `CREATING_VOLUME`/unpack-stall-under-CPU-oversubscription class has hit dozens of tests across essentially every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 (run #30), including `TestAppNICsSuite` itself in prior nights — an infrastructure/environment issue, not a product regression.
